short.EN: Multi-provider AI assistant with MCP equipment control, a local knowledge wiki it consults before answering, image analysis, and an extensible tool framework for astrophotography automation

long.EN:
Your intelligent astrophotography companion - transform NINA into a conversational, context-aware imaging system that understands your goals and helps you achieve better results.

🔭 FOR ASTROPHOTOGRAPHERS:
• Quick Session Setup: 'Set up for M31 tonight' - AI configures equipment, cooling, filters, and exposure settings
• Real-Time Troubleshooting: Analyze failed frames, high HFR, guiding issues, poor focus - get instant suggestions
• Image Quality Feedback: AI reviews your captures, identifies problems (tracking, focus, star bloat), suggests corrections
• Learning Assistant: Ask 'Why is my HFR high?' or 'Best Ha exposure for M42' - get expert guidance while imaging
• Sequence Optimization: 'Plan 4-hour session on Horsehead' - AI suggests optimal filter rotation, dither patterns, exposure times

🤖 5 AI PROVIDERS (Free to Advanced):
• Ollama (Local) - Privacy-focused, works offline, no API costs, no key
• Google Gemini - Free API tier, fast responses, MCP equipment control support
• Mistral AI - Free API tier, European-hosted models for chat, reasoning and coding
• OpenAI GPT - Most capable reasoning for complex planning
• Anthropic Claude - Best for equipment control via MCP
Dynamic model discovery ensures you always have latest AI capabilities.
(GitHub Models stays in the list for anyone who had it selected, but GitHub retired the service on July 30, 2026: it refuses every request and says which providers still work. New installations open on Ollama, the one choice that needs no API key.)

📚 KNOWLEDGE WIKI (SECOND BRAIN):
A local markdown knowledge base at %LOCALAPPDATA%\NINA\llmwiki that the assistant searches before it answers. What you know about your own rig - the focuser that needs a nudge below freezing, the flat panel that reads high with the Ha filter, the mount's habit at the meridian - takes precedence over the model's general knowledge, and the page it used is cited so you can check it.
• Seeded on first use with troubleshooting checklists and templates
• 'Remember this' saves a durable fact, always behind a confirmation dialog showing the exact text before anything is written
• Shared with AI Weather, which files a daily sky digest into the same wiki
• Plain markdown you can read and edit in any editor - nothing locked in a database

👁️ YOU CAN SEE WHAT IT IS DOING:
• Activity trace: while the assistant uses tools, a line shows the step in progress, then settles into a summary that expands into the full sequence with each call's outcome - a tool that failed or returned nothing is no longer indistinguishable from one that worked
• Context and cost readout: how full the model's context window is, the tokens used and how many are left, session totals and an estimated cost. Models whose window is unknown - local Ollama models among them - show the count without a bar rather than an invented percentage

🎛️ NATURAL LANGUAGE EQUIPMENT CONTROL (via MCP):
Control your entire observatory through conversation:
• Camera: Take exposures, adjust cooling, bin settings, gain control
• Mount: GOTO coordinates, slew, park/unpark, tracking control
• Focuser: Move absolute/relative, run autofocus, temperature compensation
• Filter Wheel: Change filters, get positions, optimize filter rotation
• Guiding: Start/stop PHD2, dither, analyze drift
• Platesolving: Solve images, sync mount, analyze pointing accuracy
150+ built-in MCP tools for complete observatory control.

📊 IMAGE ANALYSIS:
• FITS Header Reading, Star Detection, HFR/FWHM monitoring
• Statistics Analysis, Quality Assessment with actionable recommendations
• Vision API Integration for advanced image understanding

🔌 EXTENSIBLE ARCHITECTURE:
• Built-in MCP Server via NINA Advanced API plugin
• External MCP Servers for community tools
• Dynamic model discovery and custom model IDs
• Optional nina.autopilot Orchestrator dashboard integration

Transform complex equipment control and imaging workflows into simple conversations.

Changes: New icon, and the same mark in N.I.N.A.'s imaging tab strip. The old icon was white on a transparent background — it disappeared against a light theme — and the tab icon was a different drawing altogether, so the plugin looked like two plugins depending on where you saw it. Both are now the same monochrome speech bubble
FIXED: the tab icon's star was drawn on top of the bubble, and with the fill rule in use that punched a star-shaped hole in it instead of placing a star beside it

The usage readout now fits a docked panel: crammed onto the title row the three groups of figures collided and were cut off. They sit on their own labelled line that wraps with the panel width, and the provider's rate-limit budget is shown in the same compact units as everything else (12.0M rather than 11971000)

A new installation now opens on Ollama instead of GitHub Models. GitHub retired that service on 30 July 2026, so the old default meant a fresh install failed its first message with an error telling the user to change provider. Ollama is the only choice that needs no API key. Nothing changes for anyone who has already picked a provider, and GitHub stays in the list - labelled as retired - so an existing selection is not silently rewritten

The official plugin description now covers the Knowledge Wiki, the activity trace and the context and cost readout, none of which it mentioned; the retired GitHub Models service is no longer used as a search tag

Activity trace in the chat: while the assistant uses tools, a single line shows the step in progress (the tool and its arguments), then settles into a summary that expands into the full sequence with each call's outcome — a tool that failed or returned nothing is no longer indistinguishable from one that worked. Same for Claude, Gemini and Ollama; a question answered without tools leaves no trace

Context and cost readout: a bar showing how full the model's context window is (amber past two thirds, red past ninety percent), the tokens used and how many are left, plus session totals and an estimated cost. Models whose window is unknown — including local Ollama models — show the token count without a bar rather than an invented percentage

FIXED: changing the model no longer rebuilds the connection. Each settings write fired its own fire-and-forget re-initialization, and one edit writes several settings, so up to eight ran concurrently with no ordering guarantee and the surviving configuration was the one that finished last, not the one chosen last. A model change now updates the model alone; everything else is coalesced into a single initialization
FIXED: the chat header showed the previous model after picking another model of the same provider, which is what made the change look like it had not been applied
FIXED: the 'working' indicator covered the whole conversation during every request — its background stretched over the message area, so the chat looked empty until the answer arrived

Knowledge Wiki (second brain): a local markdown knowledge base (%LOCALAPPDATA%\NINA\llmwiki) the assistant searches before answering — your equipment quirks, solved problems and site notes take precedence over general knowledge, with the page used cited. Seeded on first use with troubleshooting checklists and templates; shared with AI Weather's daily sky digests and consolidated by the nina.autopilot ingest agent
'Remember this' with a real consent gate: the assistant can save durable facts to the wiki's append-only raw notes, but a confirmation dialog always shows the exact text before anything is written
New 'Disable model thinking' toggle in the Ollama options (on by default)
Options panel: checkboxes and button rows are now consistently left-aligned

Ollama: thinking-capable models (Gemma 4, Qwen 3.x, DeepSeek) were slow or returned empty replies (fixes #8) — Ollama enables a thinking phase by default, and on some runs the actual answer lands in a separate thinking field while content comes back empty. Requests now send think:false by default, and the parser recovers answers from the thinking field and strips inline think blocks
Google Gemini Test button now tests the model you selected instead of a hardcoded retired one (gemini-2.0-flash-001); all Gemini defaults use the gemini-flash-latest alias so they cannot expire again

GitHub Models provider marked as retired (fixes #7): GitHub shut the service down for everyone on July 30, 2026 - the plugin now shows a clear explanation with free alternatives (Ollama, Gemini, Mistral) instead of a raw 404
Refreshed the static Gemini fallback model list to the current generation (3.6/3.5/2.5)
Fixed MCP fetch server startup by pinning Python MCP SDK to <2.0.0 (uvx --with "mcp<2.0.0" mcp-server-fetch ...), working around the McpError -> MCPError rename in SDK 2.0.0
Fixed Mistral AI configuration section not appearing when Mistral is selected as provider (thanks @stephantamminga)
Mistral model dropdown now loads available models live from the Mistral API like the other providers
Real-time tool-calling progress feedback now shows the current iteration and tool in the chat UI
Added 90-second per-tool and 120-second external MCP read timeouts to prevent indefinite hangs
Improved Google Gemini diagnostics for HTTP errors, empty candidates, finish reasons, prompt feedback, and safety blocks
Hardened Anthropic built-in-to-external MCP routing with bounded execution and structured errors
Added the optional nina.autopilot Orchestrator integration panel
Added configurable Orchestrator URL and polling interval settings
Added optional Buy Me a Coffee project support links
Updated release metadata for the Mistral AI provider
New: full conversation history - the AI now remembers the whole chat session, so follow-up questions and 'it/that' references work (all providers)
New: external MCP tools now work with Anthropic Claude too (web fetch/search, memory, etc.), matching Gemini and Ollama
Fixed: Google Gemini 400 error - array tool parameters now correctly declare 'items' (and nested objects keep 'properties')
Fixed: changing the model now applies immediately in chat, no more switching providers back and forth
Improved: Ollama model list auto-detects installed models from the server (dropdown/Refresh re-query; re-detects when the Server URL changes)
Fixed: external MCP servers launched via npx/.cmd now start correctly on Windows (PATHEXT resolution + cmd.exe routing) - unblocks most popular MCP servers
Fixed: stdio JSON-RPC handshake corrupted by a UTF-8 BOM, which prevented strict servers (e.g. Python MCP SDK) from connecting
Fixed: concurrent external tool calls no longer collide on the server stream (serialized request/response IO)
Improved: MCP system prompt now tells the model to use available external tools (web fetch/search, etc.), not only NINA equipment tools
New: 'Useful servers' picker in Options to add fetch, search, Wikipedia, arXiv, memory and more to the config in one click
New: animated 'AI is working' indicator in chat so long tool calls don't look frozen
New: Ollama remote-host guidance for running the model on another LAN machine (OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0)
Multiple external MCP servers: connect several third-party MCP servers at once using the standard mcpServers JSON config (Google Gemini and Ollama)
External MCP servers can now use any command (python, node, npx, docker, binaries) with args and environment variables
Tool name collisions across external servers are auto-prefixed with the server name to avoid silent drops
Options UI: replaced single python/script fields with an mcpServers JSON editor plus Validate and Reset to NINA Default buttons (prefilled NINA MCP server template)
Fixed: connect/disconnect all equipment no longer falsely reports success - it now reads each device's actual API Success field and shows per-device errors
Fixed: chat input now preserves multi-line pasted text (Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline)
Backward compatible: existing single-server settings are migrated automatically
Fixed Mistral model dropdown not syncing selection to custom model textbox
Fixed Mistral provider display name showing raw enum instead of friendly name in GetProviderDisplayName
MCP support for Ollama: Local models can now control NINA equipment without paid API keys (requires tool-capable model like llama3.1+)
New Mistral AI provider: Mistral Large, Medium, Small, Mixtral, and Codestral models
MCP section now visible for Anthropic, Google, and Ollama providers
Updated provider count from 5 to 6
Profile Management: View, modify, and switch NINA profiles via conversation
Extended Sequence Control: State, edit, skip, reset, list, and set-target tools
Image Retrieval: Get captured images and thumbnails by index
Event History: Review equipment events and capture history
5 Flat Frame Tools: skyflat, auto-brightness, auto-exposure, trained-dark-flat, trained-flat
Added 7 missing equipment listing/status tools
Fixed 13 wrong API parameter names and schemas causing silent failures
Removed 6 tools mapped to non-existent API endpoints
Universal Quota Monitoring: Real-time tracking of API limits and token usage for all providers
Detailed Token Usage info in the chat header (input/output breakdown)
Proactive Rate Limit Info: Error messages now include reset times
Fixed Google Gemini MCP name collisions with built-in NINA tools
Fixed MCP status caching when switching between providers
Fixed Anthropic connection test model selection
Updated default Anthropic model to Claude 3.5 Sonnet 20241022
Improved UI header layout and stability fixes
Restructured manifest.json to match official requirements
Fixed CI/CD manifest paths
Google Gemini MCP Support
Anti-hallucination System Prompts
Dynamic Model Discovery
OpenAI Reasoning Model Support
